messages:
sarah_marketing: Quick ask for eng/runtime before we lock webinar slides: we need a trimmed, reproducible benchmark deliverable — raw outputs + perf CSVs + 1-page memo. Deadline: Mon noon PT. Can you confirm feasibility?

kevin_runtime: Feasible. Can you specify exact configs you want included (models, seqs, batches, quant)? Also where to push artifacts?

sarah_marketing: Models: redwood-v1-1b (production hash), open-llama-7b. Seq lengths: 128, 512, 2048. Batches: 1 and 16 (we're more interested in low-latency vs modest throughput). Quant: fp16 baseline + int8 if stable. Prefix cache: both ON/OFF. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, peak mem, cost-estimates. Put artifacts in s3://redwood-marketing/webinar/2026-03-bench.

ajay_ml: Add a tiny quality sanity check: run greedy decoding on 200 prompts and compute token-overlap and a simple exact-match percent on a holdout set. If int8 diverges >5% token-overlap, flag it. Also set deterministic seeds.

leo_data: I will upload a 200 prompt holdout + 200 probing prompts to s3://redwood-marketing/webinar/2026-03/payloads by EOD. Will tag prompts with short/long/complex.

kevin_runtime: Plan: run smoke matrix today on H100 and g5 (aws). Full matrix overnight: seqs 128/512/2048 × batches 1/16 × cache ON/OFF × quant fp16/int8 (skip int8 when not available). We'll produce per-run CSVs and a single summary csv. We'll include the exact docker image id and git commit sha in metadata files. Example run command (will vary per infra):

```bash
./tools/bench/run.sh \
  --model=redwood-v1-1b \
  --device=h100 \
  --seq=128 \
  --batch=1 \
  --prefix_cache=on \
  --quant=fp16 \
  --seed=202603 \
  --out=s3://redwood-marketing/webinar/2026-03/results/redwood-v1-1b/seq128-b1-cache-on/
```

kevin_runtime: We'll also push nvchaos traces and a small summary.txt that lists any ops that fell back (e.g., int8->fp16). ci-bot will enqueue jobs.

ci-bot: :gear: bench-run queued: webinar-1763999999 · watching s3://redwood-marketing/webinar/2026-03/ for artifacts

kevin_runtime: Also clarifying hardware: include on-prem H100 (our cluster), aws g5dn.12xlarge (G5) and a cheap CPU VM baseline for cost comparison. For cost-per-1M-tokens, do both on-demand and our committed-dedicated internal rate.

sarah_marketing: Legal ask: @legal_bot please flag any phrasing constraints for marketing claims. We may want to say "p95 latency as measured on our benchmark harness" instead of generic "p95 latency".

legal_bot: Noted. If you plan to publish numbers, include: (1) exact test harness link, (2) hardware and region, (3) model hashes, (4) pricing assumptions. Avoid absolute language like "fastest" unless we have head-to-head reference.

kevin_runtime: One more technical note: for streaming scenarios, we'll capture per-token latencies and end-to-end stream times. For single-shot we'll capture total generation time. Will include raw token timing logs.

tom_ops: Heads up: G5 run may be rate-limited this weekend. If we hit quotas, we'll fallback to staged runs and note that in the memo.

sarah_marketing: Acceptance criteria for marketing to publish: either p95 < 150ms for seq128 batch1 on H100 for redwood-v1-1b OR a clear comparative narrative + cost-per-1M estimate. Must include raw CSVs, run commands, and the 1-page memo (table + 3 bullets).

ajay_ml: I'll review the quality-check outputs and sign off on any int8 statements.

kevin_runtime: OK starting smoke runs now. I'll post an initial summary CSV link in this thread when smoke completes, and then the full artifact bundle when overnight jobs finish.

sarah_marketing: Thanks! Please ping when the first CSV lands. :rocket:

kevin_runtime: Will do — tagging the run with run_id=webinar-1763999999 and docker=redwood/bench:2026-03-01.

sarah_marketing: Perfect. Also if you see any flaky ops or nondeterminism, call it out so we can avoid misleading claims.

kevin_runtime: Agreed. We'll surface any nondeterminism in run_metadata.txt. :white_check_mark:
